title: Youtrip
body:
O.P.
Couldn't see a dedicated Youtrip thread so thought I'd start one up for asking my questions.
They seem quite comparable to Wise:
https://www.you.co/au/
Couldn't see any mention of temporary virtual debit cards like what Wise has but the monthly ATM withdrawal limit is a lot higher at AUD$1500 before fees kick in which makes this potentially viable for my parents' use. So I'm interested in setting this up for my parents' travels simply as a means to limit Dad's exposure of his everyday AU bank cards to potential scammers.
Got a few questions...
1. Does one need to load their Youtrip account with AUD like Wise? Or can you link Youtrip to an Aussie bank account and what ever you transact with using your Youtrip card, it can take directly from your Aussie bank account?
2. Has anyone had experience using Youtrip for WeChat pay or Alipay? Any issues? Do you still get the 2% cashback?
3. Has anyone had experience using Youtrip getting cash out in China? Any issues?
4. How have you found the exchange rate compared to the Mastercard rate?

---- replies ----
[User #8767613603 postsargamondWhirlpool Forums Addict] this post was edited
Mugsy writes...
Couldn't see a dedicated Youtrip thread so thought I'd start one up for asking my questions.
Debit card – but not on the ADI list for the financial claims scheme https://www.apra.gov.a u/list-of-authorised-deposit -taking-institutions-covered -under-financial-claims-scheme
They say that they hold an Australian Financial Services Licence, but my search using the keywords "you" or "trip" doesn't come up with their company
There are plenty of Australian listed companies that are ADIs that offer no overseas transaction fees, and you can limit risk by limiting how much you put into an account. The most popular is probably macquarie, but plenty of others (bankwest, ing, amp,...) Don't know why you would want to give your personal details and probably your money to a group that isn't really verified by APRA
[User #1114701579 postsCoops1Whirlpool Enthusiast] Why would you even want to directly link your Australian bank account to Youtrip, that's just asking for trouble!?
So many known Australian alternatives available that I wouldnt even go down this research path.
I think your creating complexity, not simplicity
[User #16843617420 postsHu_LionModerator] argamond writes...
but not on the ADI list for the financial claims scheme
That would be the same as Wise.
They say that they hold an Australian Financial Services Licence, but my search using the keywords "you" or "trip" doesn't come up with their company
The company is registered under You Technologies Group: https://service.asic.g ov.au/search/EntityDetail?Li cenceNumber=558059&Permissio nType=Australian%20financial %20services%20licensees&lice nceName=YOU%20TECHNOLOGIES%2 0GROUP%20%28AUSTRALIA%29%20PTY%20LTD
YouTrip is a Singapore based company, essentially providing a competing service to Wise. They have a strong market share in Singapore.
Coops1 writes...
Why would you even want to directly link your Australian bank account to Youtrip, that's just asking for trouble!?
It would be no different to one linking their Aussie bank account to Wise.
To clarify misconceptions here, Youtrip isn't a competitor to Australian banks with overseas ATM and foreign fee-free transactions accounts. It is a competitor to Wise.
[User #6435613504 postsMugsyEnhance your calm!Whirlpool Forums Addict] O.P.
Coops1 writes...
I think your creating complexity, not simplicity
Yeah, I came to that same conclusion about Youtrip too after some discussion on Ozbargain before you guys replied. It'll be another bloody app for Dad to have to use. He's got no interest in converting funds ahead of time. Letting the conversion happen at time of transaction and letting his funds sit in a HISA until then works for him.
argamond writes...
The most popular is probably macquarie
Dad's already with Macquarie (and ING, ubank and HSBC as back up VISA alternatives)... the problem is that he's got too many things linked to his Macquarie debit card... direct debits for electricity, internet, mobile phone annual renewals, Alipay, WeChat pay, etc, etc, and he also uses the card to pay for hotels when overseas and the card is also used for ATM withdrawals. Just takes a scammer targeting one of these and he's got issues with having to relink everything to a new debit card... which is problematic when he and mum are overseas every second month for 4-6 weeks. They could return home to their electricity and internet being cut off for example.
Of course, the simplest solution is open up another Macquarie account and move his domestic direct debits to that to silo them off from all the international travel uses.
Anyway, this probably closes out my question. The discussion has moved away from Youtrip.
[User #8767613603 postsargamondWhirlpool Forums Addict] Mugsy writes...
Dad's already with Macquarie (and ING, ubank and HSBC as back up VISA alternatives)... the problem is that he's got too many things linked to his Macquarie debit card... direct debits for electricity, internet, mobile phone annual renewals, Alipay, WeChat pay, etc, etc, and he also uses the card to pay for hotels when overseas and the card is also used for ATM withdrawals.
You can open another account and order another card. I have two cards.
Only issue is that they look the same (except the numbers), so you need to find some way to differentiate it. Alternative is to open another account from a different bank for "travel"
[User #6435613504 postsMugsyEnhance your calm!Whirlpool Forums Addict] O.P.
argamond writes...
Alternative is to open another account from a different bank for "travel"
That was one of the the reasons I initially looked into Youtrip.
But I'll go the extra transaction account route with Macquarie. He already has 2x debit cards with Macquarie (one in his name where all the current direct debits come from and links to WeChat/Alipay) and a second joint account with mum that they use as a back up when overseas if the primary card is stolen. I won't touch his current system as he's use to it.
I'll just open up a third in Dad's name that is used strictly for direct debits. He'll just keep this card stored away so that it doesn't run the risk of getting compromised. Dad just needs to make sure the funds are in this account come time of direct debit.
[User #227602206 postswildz01Forum Regular] Hu_Lion writes...
That would be the same as Wise.
Wise is listed as a registered authorised deposit-taking institution www.apra.gov.au under the "Providers of purchased payment facilties" section. They are in the same category as Paypal.
Conditions on wise banking authority www.legislation.gov.au
I assume this means they can manage claims/disputes for funds deposited, but the Australian government will not guarantee deposits up to 250k under the claims scheme, as they are not on the list of organisations covered under the claims scheme. https://www.apra.gov.au/list- of-authorised-deposit-taking -institutions-covered-under-financial-claims-scheme . Honestly who would deposit large sums permanently with Wise, as according to their conditions, they are not allowed to pay interest on deposits.
I can see no mention of Youtrip or You Technologies Pty Ltd under APRA. Does this mean there is no regulation of financial activity for Australian depositors?
[User #898936212 postsLeo HSuppository of all wisdomWhirlpool Forums Addict] wildz01 writes...
Honestly who would deposit large sums permanently with Wise, as according to their conditions, they are not allowed to pay interest on deposits.
The do pay "interest" if you let them. They invest your money and pay you a monthly return.
[User #227602206 postswildz01Forum Regular] this post was edited
Yes see that now.
This point in the legislation for Wise Australia Pty Ltd which is covered under APRA. 3. The body corporate must not pay interest on amounts held for the benefit of its customers.
Investments/Interest are by Wise Australia Investments Pty Ltd which are not covered under APRA and explicitly states this is not a deposit account under APRA.
So selecting to obtain interest must mean your money is transferred from Wise Australia Pty Ltd (APRA covered) to Wise Australia Investments Pty Ltd (which is not authorised by APRA as an authorised deposit-taking institution – ADI)
[User #585754598 postsKenjataimuWhirlpool Forums Addict] this post was edited
argamond writes...
you can open another account and order another card. I have two cards.
As do I, a platinum and a standard but they are single point of failure having Macquarie (ran into this myself some time ago, ended up they ballsed up, apologised and gave me a $250 as a sorry but only after I got back to Australia to sort it out (they cancelled both my debit cards and my Macquarie credit card and sent new ones to my home address, while I was OS) , there advice while OS was to see the Aus Embassy and see if they will give me a loan :) but that's another story) I had two backups . Coincidentally Bankwest had been closed four days before for fraud, so I used my NAB "Citi" debit card, which has since been canned by NAB so that's now out.
For me the appeal is, ever since Citbank closed, their is a dearth of multi currency accounts available, WISE, HSBC (I think) and now You stand out (are their others ?) Having a WISE account allows a USD bank account in the US, which can be used with my Charles Schwab broker for fee free transfers (either way) using pull requests via ACH. If I want to buy more using AUS, I can transfer AUD to WISE, convert to USD and have my brokerage account transfer the money fee free. I also have bond ETFs and a covered call ETP in USD with my broker that pay dividends that go into my WISE USD account and I have now started to use that USD to pay for my debit card purchases during my OS travel.
For someone who wants to use it as a travel card for a trip to Thailand or Japan once a year etc there are better options as you have said... but this is not that
[User #9418325 postsasleep-saltI'm new here, please be nice] Literally just got my Youtrip card yesterday and have been browsing forums to see what people reckon about it. I'll be testing it out on a couple of short trips soon.
been thinking of keeping some GBP in my Youtrip account since the pound has been dipping before my next trip to london end of the year. Anyone been using Youtrip regularly over the last few months?
[User #1610139005 postsPhil TThe only constant is changeSection Moderator] asleep-salt writes...
Anyone been using Youtrip regularly over the last few months?
Not exactly with regularity (just a few online USD purchases), but one of the appeals is a higher fee-free withdrawal limit compared to the likes of Wise and Revolut [base tier], and a slightly better exchange rate. This would be of more appeal if you had the funds in a specific currency (eg. USD or HKD) vs using the likes of a debit card from Macquarie/ING/Up/etc and getting the rate as set by Visa/Mastercard at the time of withdrawal, so each to themselves on that one.
One new feature they did add is the ability to add funds via PayID [they generate an ID for you] and a BSB/account number now – previously this was restricted to loading from a debit (and credit?) card. (I've only tried transferring funds from my home ANZ bank account, and not say from Wise etc – which you would still only be able to transfer AUD as Youtrip can only accept funds in your home currency, typically AUD).
[User #4587512303 poststak1990Whirlpool Forums Addict] this post was edited
Just came back from Bali and used the youtrip card quite heavily with no issues. It gave me an notification in IDR and AUD everytime i use it which is quite handy. I had my money in AUD and paid in IDR everytime so it auto converted. Now that I’m back I noticed I can’t transfer money out of my youtrip account into my bank account…… Seems like the only way is to withdraw in cash and deposit into my bank account…
I guess im going back to Wise for the convenience, the fees on wise is low enough for the convenience it provides.
[User #6435613504 postsMugsyEnhance your calm!Whirlpool Forums Addict] O.P.
tak1990 writes...
Now that I’m back I noticed I can’t transfer money out of my youtrip account into my bank account…… Seems like the only way is to withdraw in cash and deposit into my bank account…
Yes, this seems to be a drawback with Youtrip at the moment. It's either withdraw as cash or spend the remaining funds whether here or overseas (the latter may not be a bad idea if you still have the 2% cashback).
If I was getting a Youtrip account, I would do what you did and keep the funds in AUD and NOT put too much money on the Youtrip card trying to use all the funds by the end of the trip. I'd only be getting it for the 2% cashback.
Otherwise, I'd just do what my folks do and use their Macquarie debit cards when overseas... great rates and saves them the hassle of moving funds around.
